items.claim: G19 covers every declared copy and root
items.evidence: Lines 770–792 traverse names_exact plus names_normalised, hash every member, and recompute distinct digest counts. Independently verified 45+45 groups, 60+377=437 member visits, 377 unique paths matching scan_bounds.files_hashed=377, with no digest/count mismatches. Instrumented execution confirmed 437 member reads, only 24 root isdir calls, and zero root walks, despite reporting '25 roots re-checked'. An in-memory replacement of sources_31.path with a nonexistent path still returned OK. Chapter 14.3 also claims undeclared-copy discovery, which this function does not implement.

notes: No repairs or filesystem writes were performed. Python was unavailable on PATH; execution used the installed Codex-runtime Python with bytecode disabled. Both gate entry points were executed through runpy with the requested arguments under an audit guard blocking writes and subprocess creation. This was necessary because ordinary gate execution invokes G22 -> selftest_diagnose -> a subprocess whose selftest writes and restores artifacts (lines 1339–1351). The guard blocked that subprocess before launch; therefore the maker's unrestricted runs were NOT_VERIFIABLE, and guarded results must not be represented as exact reproductions. Observed round line: 'VERDICT PASS pass=16/18 blocking_fail=0 open_reporting=2 hygiene=0'. Observed payload line: 'VERDICT PASS pass=12/13 blocking_fail=0 open_reporting=1 hygiene=0'. Both returned exit 0; G22 reported CHECK_RAISED because of the guard. Payload scope excludes G11, G13, G16a, G16b, and G19. These exclusions are stored in the internal report's excluded_in_this_scope field but are NOT announced in stdout by the requested command without --json. The payload gate source differs from the round source only in line endings. The supplied payload gate/GATE_R13.json records a full round-scope run, not the requested payload-scope run. Member hashing is repaired; the all-roots claim remains false.
